title: Fix the invalidation in update_email
problem: users.py caches users in Redis. get_user is correct, but update_email has three bugs: readers keep seeing the old email, the invalidation happens at the wrong moment, and when Redis is down nobody ever finds out. Fix update_email.
requirements: Delete the same key that get_user reads (use user_key)
Delete it only after the UPDATE is committed
If there is no such user, raise UserNotFound
If the delete fails because of Redis (redis.RedisError), don't fail the update: it is committed. Log a warning on the 'users' logger that names the key
Don't catch anything broader than redis.RedisError, so real bugs still surface
contract: update_email(conn: sqlite3.Connection, r, user_id: int, email: str) -> None   # raises UserNotFound
expectedBehavior: get_user(conn, r, 1) caches {'id': 1, 'email': 'old@x.io'}; after update_email(conn, r, 1, ' New@X.io ') the next get_user returns {'id': 1, 'email': 'new@x.io'}. A second database connection already sees 'new@x.io' at the moment the cache key is deleted.
edgeCases: A concurrent reader between the delete and the commit (the test checks what another connection sees at delete time)
Redis unreachable after the commit: the update still succeeds and a warning names cache:user:<id>
A non-Redis exception from the client (a bug) must propagate
hints: Conceptual: the database is the truth and the cache is a copy. Deleting the copy before the truth changes lets a reader refill the copy with the old value. And an error you swallow is an outage nobody can see.

Specific: compare the key update_email deletes with the key get_user reads. Then move the delete below the `with conn:` block. Finally, replace the bare `except Exception: pass` with something narrower that leaves a trace.
Implementation: after the with block and the rowcount check, key = user_key(user_id); try: r.delete(key) except redis.RedisError as e: log.warning('cache invalidation failed for %s: %s', key, e).
evaluation: The cache key is built only by user_key
The delete runs after the commit, and its failure is logged with the key, not swallowed
